source_title: James May Drove Slate's Tiny Electric Truck And Says He'd Buy One: Video
source_excerpt:
After driving Slate's tiny pickup, James May said he could be a customer.
Slate’s tiny new truck is getting a lot of attention, and for good reason. With an estimated starting price of around $25,000, a stripped-down interior, and a simple electric powertrain, the company is betting that buyers will embrace a back-to-basics approach to pickup ownership—especially when everything is so expensive.
One of those buyers could be James May . The Top Gear legend and gin aficionado recently got behind the wheel of a Slate truck, and he had plenty to say about the pint-sized pickup. For the most part, he was impressed.
In fact, when May considered whether he would actually buy one, his answer was pretty definitive: "You know what, I think I would—I’d have one." Quite an endorsement from someone who's driven just about everything on the planet. Watch the full video below:
The Slate isn't exactly a traditional pickup, but its unusual approach could be exactly what appeals to buyers like May.
The truck features a compact two-seat cabin, a small cargo bed, and an all-electric powertrain with a single rear-mounted motor. Slate estimates it will deliver around 150 miles of range on a charge, with an available larger battery potentially increasing that figure to approximately 240 miles.
There are manual windows, physical controls, and a straightforward dashboard. Heck, there isn't even a standard infotainment screen. Instead, Slate provides a simple phone mount, leaving drivers to use their own devices for navigation and entertainment.
Whether that minimalist approach and relatively affordable price tag will be enough to make the Slate a success remains to be seen. But if May's reaction is any indication, Slate might actually be onto something. At least… for a certain kind of buyer.
